title: CV Tutorial — source verification for chapters 01–05
scope: Original method definitions, official API contracts and deterministic toy experiments. All synthetic examples are illustrative, not benchmark reproductions.

entries.claim: OpenCV image matrices use row/column/channel indexing and default BGR order for common color reads
entries.locator: Operations with images: BGR ordering and img[y,x]
entries.notes: RGB is a generic image convention; OpenCV BGR must be called out separately.

entries.claim: Classification, object detection and semantic segmentation have different output spaces and annotation granularity
entries.locator: Mask R-CNN introduction and task distinctions
entries.notes: This is a conceptual task taxonomy, not a model leaderboard.

entries.claim: Intersection over Union is intersection area divided by union area
entries.locator: Jaccard similarity coefficient
entries.notes: Empty-union handling depends on the evaluation protocol.

entries.claim: Mean IoU averages class-level IoU values over the classes included by an evaluation protocol
entries.locator: Evaluation API and category-wise evaluation conventions
entries.notes: Do not silently count absent classes as zero or one.

entries.claim: ImageNet introduced a large-scale hierarchical labeled image database
entries.locator: Deng et al., CVPR 2009, dataset construction
entries.notes: Historical dataset contribution; not a current model benchmark.

entries.claim: AlexNet combined a deep convolutional network, large labeled data and GPU training for ImageNet classification
entries.locator: Krizhevsky et al. 2012, architecture and experiments
entries.notes: No paper metric is copied into the toy code.

entries.claim: The Vision Transformer applies a Transformer encoder to patch-tokenized image inputs
entries.locator: Dosovitskiy et al., abstract and Section 3
entries.notes: The original preprint date and later conference publication should not be conflated.

entries.claim: OpenCV imread with color mode returns a BGR color image; channel order matters for conversion
entries.locator: Operations with images: BGR channel order
entries.notes: A channel-order mistake changes colors and any color-dependent preprocessing.

entries.claim: OpenCV provides explicit BGR-to-gray conversion through cvtColor
entries.locator: Color conversion codes: COLOR_BGR2GRAY
entries.notes: Displayed coefficients are explanatory; use the library conversion routine.

entries.claim: Gaussian and other low-pass filters smooth local image variations; border handling is part of the operator contract
entries.locator: Smoothing Images; filter2D and borderType
entries.notes: Synthetic output counts are not asserted across every OpenCV build.

entries.claim: Canny includes noise smoothing, gradient estimation, non-maximum suppression and hysteresis thresholding
entries.locator: Canny theory steps 1–5
entries.notes: The OpenCV L2gradient flag changes gradient magnitude convention.

entries.claim: Opening is erosion followed by dilation; closing is dilation followed by erosion
entries.locator: Morphological transformations: opening and closing
entries.notes: Effect depends on foreground polarity and structuring element.

entries.claim: NumPy gradient returns derivatives in axis order and uses central differences internally with one-sided boundary differences
entries.locator: numpy.gradient: return order and finite-difference scheme
entries.notes: For a 2D array, first output is row-axis derivative, second is column-axis derivative.

entries.claim: SIFT uses scale-space extrema, keypoint localization, orientation assignment and local gradient descriptors
entries.locator: Lowe 2004, Sections 3–6
entries.notes: Rotation and scale normalization do not imply invariance to arbitrary viewpoint or occlusion.

entries.claim: OpenCV SIFT exposes create/detectAndCompute and the default descriptor uses 128 dimensions
entries.locator: cv::SIFT class reference; Python create overloads
entries.notes: The deterministic synthetic test checks non-empty descriptors and shape, not detection quality.

entries.claim: HOG aggregates gradient-orientation histograms in cells, normalizes overlapping blocks and concatenates a window descriptor
entries.locator: Dalal and Triggs, CVPR 2005, descriptor and detector
entries.notes: The 36-dimensional block is only a 2×2-cell, 9-bin example.

entries.claim: An integral image permits an axis-aligned rectangle sum from four prefix-sum values
entries.locator: Viola and Jones, CVPR 2001, integral image
entries.notes: This chapter uses inclusive coordinates and defines out-of-range prefix values as zero.

entries.claim: Viola–Jones combines Haar-like features, feature selection and a cascade to reject easy negative windows early
entries.locator: Viola and Jones, CVPR 2001, cascade classifier
entries.notes: This is the original face detection framework, not every modern cascade.

entries.claim: Reverse-mode automatic differentiation records executed operations and applies the chain rule backward through the graph
entries.locator: Autograd mechanics: how autograd encodes history
entries.notes: The scalar example is an analytical toy, not a neural-network training benchmark.

entries.claim: Gradient contributions from multiple uses of a shared intermediate are accumulated during backpropagation
entries.locator: Autograd mechanics: disallowing implicit gradient accumulation
entries.notes: The graph figure illustrates a general reverse-mode dependency rule.

entries.claim: PyTorch CrossEntropyLoss accepts unnormalized logits and class-index targets for the standard multiclass case
entries.locator: Input and Target shape / class-index formulation
entries.notes: The stable NumPy example subtracts max(logits) before exponentiation.

entries.claim: ReLU is non-differentiable at zero and automatic differentiation frameworks define a usable subgradient convention
entries.locator: Autograd mechanics: gradients for non-differentiable functions
entries.notes: The article's slider uses a zero derivative at the kink as its declared convention.

entries.claim: PyTorch Conv2d computes valid 2D cross-correlation over NCHW input with a weight tensor organized by output and input channels
entries.locator: Conv2d description and input/weight/output shapes
entries.notes: The word convolution is retained as the common framework layer name.

entries.claim: Conv2d output dimensions depend on input size, kernel, stride, padding and dilation with integer floor behavior
entries.locator: Dumoulin and Visin, convolution arithmetic output-size formulas
entries.notes: The simple formula assumes explicit symmetric numeric padding.

entries.claim: A standard groups=1 Conv2d weight tensor has Cout×Cin×Kh×Kw weights and optional Cout biases
entries.locator: Conv2d weight and bias shapes
entries.notes: Parameter count does not equal FLOPs or end-to-end latency.

entries.claim: The theoretical receptive field grows recursively with kernel size and cumulative stride
entries.locator: CS231n convolution arithmetic and receptive field discussion
entries.notes: Theoretical support does not imply uniform effective influence.
